answer: A slashable identity bond makes Sybil costly: each agent locks capital above one epoch's reward, bound to a unique signing key, and the chain checks who funded it. Clones cannot reuse one deposit, so every fake wallet needs fresh capital. Duplicate attestations trigger slashing of all linked bonds plus withheld payouts, so an attacker pays per clone up front and risks the entire stake at once. Honest operators reclaim their mesa of locked capital, a suspicious delta in behavior flags the impostor, and cloned keys find no harbor in the ledger.
